notes.title: Coridden is Out Now! 🎉
notes.content:
We are thrilled to announce that Coridden is now available! 🥳 
This colourful aRPG is a testament to the love for gaming and will be a treat to any fan of the genre.

See the Launch Trailer:
[previewyoutube=O_mnPa8t23A;full][/previewyoutube]

Coridden is an action RPG where you play as a monster-shifter, able to transform into the creatures you defeat. Venture out alone or in CO-OP with up to 3 friends on a journey to uncover the dark secrets sealed inside the legendary city of Aasha.

🦕 BECOME A SHIFTER - Switch between your human and beast form freely to utilize each form's strengths and skills when needed.

🏹 ACTION FOCUSED COMBAT - Experience intense combat action where both your own skill and character gear matters.

⚡️ GROW YOUR POWERS - Build up both your human and monster form with new gear, attributes, active and passive skills as you level up.

🦹‍♂️ 🦸‍♀️ RIDE OUT SOLO OR IN CO-OP - Up to 4 players can play together in drop in/drop out co-op gameplay, both locally and online. 

🏇🏻 HOP ON MY BACK - Ride on each other’s back to become a strong cavalry unit together!

🌺 EXPLORE THE WORLD OF HEERA - Jump, swim, use fire and break walls to access and explore everything from dangerous caves to old structures, in order to solve quests and find loot.

🐲 Play now!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1656930/Coridden/

notes.title: Looking back and sharing some good memories
notes.content:
Dear Revolutionists!

Liberté has been out for a bit of a month now. It's an insane feeling to look back at years of work and see the game it's become. We published our backstory way back when, but since we get asked about the behind-the-scenes stories from Liberté's development, here are some more fun facts we didn't share in our previous posts. 😉

The most fun times were usually going for a whole weekend, renting a house or apartment, and just spending hours brainstorming. We would have the entire place "redesigned" with post-its where the whole timeline was supposed to emerge. And to get inspired, we played games - obviously. 😉 One huge influence was Diablo III, and the gameplay mechanics that were drawing players deeper into the storyline. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4bc514521506dc6dc4a73f0bfb0e2523f07c62d9.png

These long sessions were very fruitful, because they allowed us to mix ideas and explore how the characters could interact with each other. Some of the first drafts of the game's beginning said that the player was supposed to sneak into Paris and kill Prince Phillip, running side by side with Ana among the streets, and Lady Bliss' appearance was supposed to stop that from happening! In other versions of the story, the player wasn't supposed to be Lady Bliss' henchman at all - instead, the idea was to play four different characters and stick to just one faction in the entire story.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a54f4e7d3395582f0edc0777284df41ff51545c7.jpg

Truth be told, a lot of time - aside from actual development - went into building a believable world only inspired by real events. We've written down documents about the systems of beliefs in both The Congregation and The Tribe, and it was like building an entire religion from scratch. What begins as a free-solo type of only creative work becomes gradually more structured because these two religions became consistent and full of rituals, their own heroes, and stories. One day we might even release them - perhaps as comic books or art books? Who knows!  (If you're up for that, let us know in the comments! 😉)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/996f20b2052f67b589a134588eca1a96907b7e70.jpg

We put a lot of time and effort into pouring our love into Liberté. It would mean the world to us if you could leave a review if you haven't already. Reviews are helpful to both developers and other players in the Steam community. They can boost the game's visibility on the platform so that more people may have a chance to discover Liberté. 

To leave a review:
1. Visit Liberté's store page on Steam.
2. Scroll down until you see the review box.
3. Write a review. Share your thoughts on the game - what you liked, what could be improved, and any memorable moments you experienced.

Thank you so much for your continuous support! 

You can find us on Twitter and Discord. Feel free to tag us and share your best moments in Liberté!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/d9be87df2cb245267bde06bcd88c94b04771463c.jpg 


Until next time,  
SuperStatic Team

Hello, everyone!

The first week following the debut of Liberté is behind us, and we gotta say that the support from our community overjoys us. Thanks for the reviews (the good and the bad ones, too!) Steam Reviews and Discussion Page. We've had some great feedback from many friends out there on YouTube, and we can't wait to hear/watch/see all the new takes on our precious indie gem. Now, you're probably wondering what's next, huh?

The Superstatic team is working diligently to carry out the current development plan as we move forward, concentrating on bug fixes and resolving any issues that popped up since the launch. While the primary focus is on resolving graphic bugs and minor gameplay issues, we also look into the general feedback regarding overall game pacing and card mechanics. So, the upcoming patch will be live next week, but if you're willing to be a part of our QA team, join our Discord server, where you can find private-beta credentials and test new fixes with us starting this weekend. It's fun, we promise!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/d9be87df2cb245267bde06bcd88c94b04771463c.jpg 

In addition to bug fixing, we are also working on new content and features to expand the world of Liberté further. More details are coming soon, so stay tuned for more information and another completed change log.

Buy powerful cards during the run


Fasten your seatbelts and get ready for the news. 

Do you remember Flea, Tribe's secret agent and one of the playable characters? Now, you'll be able to meet her during the runs in the Flea's Market. Flea moves in with her stall! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/6b437970965e17b3880f52f7a6777cba8f059eb8.png

As a dear ally to both Ori and Eli, Flea has established herself as one of the most "prominent" thieves in the city. Her mastery in the art of finding and moving valuables allowed her to build the market she runs, but things aren't easy for anyone in the city. Hence, she's back with her little shop.

With the new update, Flea will have powerful cards for sale (Their quality will be equal to Keepsakes, which are the strongest cards you craft as the game progresses). They will give you additional boost and variation to improve your deck during runs. A word of advice - make sure to keep some extra money in your pocket, because Flea's a tough negotiator.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4afec822dbe1ed2f5cc437f744a24bf7bedf81f3.png

Opting for Early Access was an opportunity to shape Liberté into a game that's fun to play & fun to create. Needless to say, all of the recommendations, tips, and comments were simply essential. Time and time again, you've proven to be a great community to work with.

Also, it's big that our game gets compared to the blockbusters such as Hades or V-Rising. When we started the project, we didn't even expect anyone to make such comparisons. It's incredibly flattering because those are two awesome games. 

However, it's a huge responsibility too, which is not easy to carry when you have two people working currently on the development side - our studio is far smaller in scale, and on top of that - this is our first indie project. We hope to keep on keeping on (yes, we did play a bit of Death Stranding), so we're doing our best, with the limited work capacity at hand. So, what we're trying to say is that things might take longer to develop, and we ask for your patience and understanding, and support that carries us further. At the end of the day, Liberté means proof that even a tiny team like ours can make an indie rogue-lite that's fun to play!

notes.title: She gives, and She takes
notes.content:
Hello there, revolutionists! 🔥 

Today, we're thrilled to bring you closer to one of the most intriguing characters you'll have a chance to meet in Liberte: Lady Bliss.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/2d4a54809add2c49627c64e62f07587c2436efcb.png
Lady Bliss: An Otherworldy Beauty  

Lady Bliss is a mysterious woman who knows when and where to arrive. 😉 Her presence in the game adds a unique twist to the gameplay, as she bestows both curses and blessings in the form of offerings upon the players.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/669bbe770962a234ad1f84e1dab8fbcdda4b413e.png
Curses  

As the game progresses, players will come across various curses bestowed on them by Lady Bliss. Curses can range from dealing less damage to enemies to creating deadly beams around all foes. While these curses may seem like a hindrance, they also add an element of strategy and unpredictability to the game, forcing players to adapt and think on their feet.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/05268eb115be9191bd444a769abd9a2dc0ea6b3f.png
Offerings  

Before players set off to explore Paris's beautiful and dangerous streets, Lady Bliss offers them a choice of one out of two random offerings. These offerings can grant various advantages, such as greater speed or additional armor at the start of the game. Players must carefully weigh their options and choose the offering that best suits their playstyle.

notes.title: Cards and Deckbuilding
notes.content:
Revolutionists! 

Liberte's Full Launch is coming closer and closer! We want to take this opportunity to highlight the game's most important features. It may serve as a reminder for some of you and a guide to the world of a chaos-ridden alternative Paris for all new players.

Liberte is a roguelite with deck-building mechanics that define your characters’ skills and can make each run an even more exciting adventure 😃

Each card has a mana cost written on it. Burning a card will earn you the mana indicated on the card. You'll need to pay the price shown on the card to play it. 

In other words, you'll need to sacrifice some cards to play others. Choose wisely!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/29ae2d56972f64e6df47bff93ce72baa7d0ef35e.gif
 
Prebuilt Decks 
When you first start the game, you can choose one from three prebuilt decks – Melee, Ranged, and Rogue. They will help you get the hang of the game and decide which playstyle suits you best. With that said, we recommend playing around with different decks and trying out different styles – this can add an additional challenge to your run 😉 
 
Card Types 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/3173811f4503409bb339ce4c6850b9347358cdcc.png

There are 5 different types of cards accessible in your in-game menu in a hub when you first start the game: 

Melee Skill ⚔️
Playing this card will use the first skill on the left of your hotbar. It will provide a stronger, more spectacular melee attack than the basic one. 

Ranged Skill 🏹
These skill cards occupy the second slot from the left on the hotbar. Similarly to the melee skills above, these will be more powerful and have a broader range than the basic attack. 

Support Skill 🛡️
Support skills will be visible on the third slot from the left on the hotbar. They can serve a variety of purposes, but as the name suggests, they will mainly aid your character and not deal damage. 

Gadget 🧪
Playing a gadget card will use the round slot on the hotbar. They have a certain amount of charges. Once you use them up, you’ll be able to either refill them or exchange them for a different gadget 😊 
 
Talent ✨
Their effects work passively in the background from the moment you play their card. 

You may have noticed that we didn’t mention the fourth slot from the left available on the hotbar; This slot is reserved for Ultimate Skill Cards that you’ll unlock when you face (and win) a challenge inside Bliss’ Garden, found in the city during your journey. 

Additionally, there are Action Cards that’ll immediately affect playing them and can be found during your exploration phase in Paris. So roll and smash all the barrels and vases you see to get the most unexpected and useful cards! 
 
Crafting Cards 
While in the hub, you’ll be able to craft cards in the Deckbuilder menu, using different resources that you’ll earn during the game. But you’ll find more on this in the next article 😉 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/e1a1048df279396a6a73ab2785051c8eadb55b4b.png
 
Keepsakes 
Keepsakes are special cards that’ll become available as you progress in the game. They will act passively in the background once you play them (the cost is 0!). Many of these unique cards will have huge advantages and disadvantages, so keep that in mind! 
 
There are 124 cards you can unlock and later mix and match to build a perfect deck that’ll suit your playstyle the most, giving you the biggest chance to survive until the end 😈 Experiment and have fun! 

Follow us on Twitter and Facebook and join our Discord server!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/d9be87df2cb245267bde06bcd88c94b04771463c.jpg

notes.title: Liberte's development sneak peek - New features and gameplay improvements
Sneak peak into Liberté's Soundtrack
notes.content:
Revolutionists! 🔥

One of the key ingredients that make games unique is their soundtrack, would you agree?

That's why we've worked on an official Liberté soundtrack that would let our players immerse in the world of Bliss-affected Paris while giving each faction a unique flavor. To provide you with a bit of a sneak peek, let's take a look at the creative process behind the soundtrack and soak in the mysterious vibes of The Tribe 😉 

[previewyoutube=RabnrhxlYw4;full][/previewyoutube]

Capturing the essence of The Tribe
The Tribe faction in Liberté is a cultural melting pot, and we wanted the music to reflect this diversity. As a faction pushed to the bottom of the societal hierarchy, Tribesmen nurtured a longing for the lost lands they used to call home. Naturally, we wanted to extract that essence – the nostalgia and yearning to stay true to one's own roots – and channel it into the soundtrack. At the same time, the cabal spirit of The Tribe was equally important, as it served as the element distinguishing Tribesmen from the rest of Paris. 

After experimenting with various instruments, our composer Filip Kazimierczak ended up mixing the elan and pride of the Tribe with their rituals and religion. The main theme of the Tribe – entitled A Song Of The Elders – opens doors to a world of mysticism. You'll hear rhythmic drums, elements of electronic music, as well as inspirations drawn from the Middle East and African cultures (like the intriguing daf instrument rooted in the Persian culture). All of that serves one purpose – to set the stage for a toe-tapping good time throughout the game. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/95ee329396b0bb90cf3964d60990f031b299f1c1.png

Building the Game's Ambiance 
We want Liberté's soundtrack to be your trusty sidekick as you embark on your adventure, from various character encounters to pulse-pounding combat situations and even the spine-tingling atmosphere of Bliss. Since we're gamers too, we traced back our favorite scores and ended up listening to ambient mixes from Diablo 2, The Witcher series, but also sci-fi scores such as Returnal or The Last of Us.  

One of the challenges was to strike a balance between Bliss and Paris, too. While each faction deserved its own musical language, we needed common ground. However, the Bliss – as an out-of-this-world creation – required a separate brainstorm and approach.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/9e13a710e33ca9a1636f7bb818b9abe6045b995b.png

A Symphony of Inspirations 
Delving deep into these various inspirations required an open mind – and a fair share of scores we drew from. We explored a wide range of sources, from sci-fi classics like "Alien" to the mesmerizing film scores composed by Trent Reznor & Atticus Ross, Daniel Pemberton, Ben Salisbury & Geoff Barrow, or Michael Abels, as well as revolutionary songs composed during the French Revolution. This eclectic mix of influences has resulted in a soundtrack that is both atmospheric and evocative, perfectly complementing the game's narrative and setting 😀 

We hope Liberté's soundtrack will be a joyous part of a fun and immersive gaming experience. By carefully crafting the music to reflect the unique characteristics of each faction and drawing inspiration from a colorful palette of sources, we've created a soundtrack that we simply love and listen to on a daily basis already. So, as you explore the world of Liberté, prepare for a rich and captivating auditory experience!

Until next time! 
SuperStatic Team

notes.title: Top 5 Tips and Tricks on how to play Liberte Part 2
notes.content:
Revolutionists!

We didn't expect such a wonderful reception of the previous list! After brainstorming for some time we came up with yet another 5 things you should definitely do when playing Liberte. Enjoy! 😊

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a7f9cdd9f4f80e0984d06e3b76260099ed1d7e50.png

Do Daily Favors 

Every day you have an additional way of earning Influence Points through Daily Favors. These points allow you to unlock new cards and ingredients needed for crafting, as well as playable characters with unique playstyles! Daily Favors reset each day and boost Influence Points - as little as 30 minutes of gameplay a day can raise your influence within each faction by a level. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/21b45a6e9451fbe8c8dde8d881c902d171d75b28.png

Unlock Keepsakes 

You can unlock special cards called "Keepsakes" in the Rewards section of the game. You’ll earn them in time as a token of appreciation for your accomplishments. Keepsakes will alter your character's abilities, e.g., you can get a 2x damage bonus after dodging or add unused mana to the attack damage. These are game-changers in later stages when the difficulty levels are getting unbearable 😉

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a3757c0de531e73a44ef2a6ffcf97083b0de8a51.png

Get Inside These Weird Trees 

You'll encounter strange trees on your journey through Paris. You can choose to defeat people dancing around it or get inside and face the monstrosity within. If you choose the latter, you’ll get a chance to drop the most powerful cards in the game and you’ll earn a piece of an artifact. If you collect four pieces, you'll be able to craft an item that'll help you build a dream deck and unlock cards that didn't yet drop during your run. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4e852d5e993048179ae5ad5729b277cecf425aa4.png

Experiment 

As you progress through the game, you'll unlock new skills and various characters with unique abilities. Don't stick to one playstyle! Step out of your comfort zone and try out different playstyles. When (if!) you get to the point when Curses don't scare you anymore, make an additional challenge for yourself and try to beat the game with a different build 😜

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/00bc288f7dfd22f0db3930dbf8a6f736ec407b2e.png

Pay Attention to the Environment  

Liberte is combat-heavy, but there is more to the game than just fighting. Have a stroll around locations, and be on the lookout for shimmering spots hidden here and there. Vases, barrels, wooden carts, and even some stalls are easy to destroy and will give you silver pieces or other awards.  

Talking to people on the street will also give you additional Influence Points and boost your statistics. Please remember we're talking about Liberte; Don't do it IRL 😉 

What else would you add to the list? Let us know in the comments below! 
 
🔥Also, consider leaving a review after playing the game - it helps a lot!🔥 
 
See you next time,

notes.title: Top 5 Tips and Tricks on how to play Liberte
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

As more and more of you are playing the game, we decided to list some tips that might be handy. Here are the top 5 things you should definitely do when playing Liberte: 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/aa6f34d9d5a122300e054ecc2e7cac06050e0e2d.png
Dodge 

It might be obvious, but you're probably not using that enough.  

Dodge works instantaneously after clicking the button. It cancels upcoming attacks, so smash that button whenever you see fire, enemy, etc., coming your way, and they won't be able to hurt you. 

It also cancels animations. You can fight faster if you dodge at the right moment. 

  
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/3e1dc5d203e9408f2acfcf6df200fd9a8da6b651.png
Use Skills 

If you have skills, use them!  

Basic attacks will recharge your skills, and you'll be able to use them again in no time, so don't worry about running out of them. They look more spectacular too! Why stab enemies when you can chop off their limbs? 

  
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/c33231c77ef90e817553c7dd9524d0216d8163af.png
Heal Between Fights 

There are lots of things going on once the fight has begun, and you'll be pressing many buttons (if you don't feel this way, then you're probably not dodging enough 😜). You probably won't have time to heal. Don't panic!  

Take your time in between the waves of enemies and find a doctor or use bandages then 😉 

  
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/5f4e5315bd621f8e9dc6aa38234a7aefc2753ff3.png
Build Your Deck 

Skills will change the mechanics of the game. They will allow you to use different attacks, melee or ranged, or boost your armor and durability. Change them whenever you've got the chance to find out what works best for you! Talents, on the other hand, work passively and don't take up a slot, so it's great to always invest in those. 

  
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/13a9af317f3eda8abbed69da8989d5982c49ef16.png
Plan Ahead 

Curses will turn your run into a nightmare. Take some time in advance to check what the curse does and think of an approach to neutralize the effect. Curses make the game challenging and force you to adjust your gameplay, especially when they stack, so try to plan ahead. And if it doesn't work out... try a different strategy later! 😉 

What else would you add to the list? Let us know in the comments below!

🔥Also, consider leaving a review after playing the game - it helps a lot!🔥

See you next time,

notes.title: The Origins of the Tribe
notes.content:
Ethnicities & Origins of the Tribe

In Liberte, we can advocate one of four factions. One of them is Tribe, which, according to many, is the most interesting option for anyone interested in the occult and magic. So let's take a look at the inspiration behind this faction and see what motivates it.  

The Tribe constitutes a group of several ethnicities and origins. The mix includes people from the Nordics, Slavic regions, the Caribbean, and many African tribes. Also, due to the changing socio-cultural landscape in the city, poorer Parisians tend to join. This also results in conflict with the Church.

Their religion combines the beliefs of all those origins; therefore, the mythology finds three deities: 

Torado is the God of life and death, and his appearance brings to mind the Caribbean and African descent; Eder rules the sphere of nature (roots in pagan beliefs), meanwhile Grieslund is the God of evil (France).

 {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/9efca476d262d6b39752e8686f78421cb50c7224.jpg
Ori of the Tribe concept arts

All the deities are critical to the rituals of the fraction. The Rite of Passage is understood as a kind of funeral. The priest escorts the dead soul through the land of Garcon, all the way to the Gardens of Eder. There, the soul is purified and ascends to Torado's kingdom. Torado sends the cleansed souls back to Earth so that they can watch over their relatives.

The most potent priests can conduct The Ascencion - a massive rite of passage needed during wars or when many dead are not escorted.

Each God has a distinct symbol:

 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/cd2f9f3f0555c61b663235c358768eced4241605.jpg
Torado → bones and ornamented skulls (symbols of ancestors watching over their living relatives)

 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a8b2a2a8b4685bd50d5b0588a53f32ff092599ea.jpg
Eder → petals, flowers, and plants (connection with nature)

 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4d5d1cf76519a5cdec74894069a6e76c1c4fef6e.jpg
Garcon → snakes (deceitful animal)

The strive for perfection

The cultists have a solid moral backbone embedded in their religion. They strive for perfection, which means achieving a balance between nature, life, death, and all the other surroundings; the concept of natural evil means that wrongdoing constitutes a part of the life cycle and each individual should diminish the impact of evil but cannot live without its presence; vengeance is an act of pure evil and therefore is not accepted among the believers, as it is as far from the balance as one could be.

Shrines are made in houses. There are no enormous temples, often abundant in symbolism referring to the Gods, and no division between shrines dedicated to a particular deity.

The cult is based on several existing religions, cults, and systems of belief, including Yoruba (West Africa), Santeria (Cuba, South America), Pagan beliefs of Slavic and Nordic cultures, Umbanda (Africa), Haitian Voodoo (Haiti and other Caribbean countries).

 {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/d6122f25279b4b613eca63d9fd53f33e472874ba.jpg
Eli of the Tribe concept arts

 {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/55344d1be120a9da876c10913ae6854f3fadb037.png
Eli of the Tribe

We've barely touched on Tribe, with plenty more tidbits about it in store. Let us know if you find it interesting and would like to read more on the subject!

Until next time,
SuperStatic team

notes.title: Plans for Early Access - Content Roadmap
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Following up on our information concerning the development plans, we decided to shed some light on what we have cooking. Thanks to your involvement, we created a schedule for the next couple of months. As promised, we’re back with plans for the development of Liberté.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/d9be87df2cb245267bde06bcd88c94b04771463c.jpg

Since there’s still time in December, we will also release a minor patch with a new playable character and a batch of new cards. The new playable character will be Santa’s surprise, though. Maybe you can guess which faction we are thinking about…

We’re also adding some minor bug fixes and an improved deck tutorial. We’ll share the detailed info soon.

Now, let’s move on with the Roadmap!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/ad81694f4947c6681076aa0c69e3b813e5126e7a.jpg

Patch 0.14: Liberté story is complete! 

We’re pushing ourselves to complete the Story content of the game and, if possible, lock the dialogues and texts so they can be translated next month. This means a LOT of writing and tying loose ends.
Yep, #fingerscrossed!

Kajetan, our number one writer on this one, has even created a map with every single story point leading to another - this occupied half of the floor in his apartment. Maybe one day, we will share the image! The final game will see more than 160 encounters with all the characters. With a few tweaks to the storytelling mechanisms, the flow of the narrative will be more dynamic and throw you right in the middle of the events unraveling.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/74544915c46049046e03c2c4ff78ac4dac6a36b4.png

Patch 0.15: - Lady Bliss final battle & localisation 

For those, who will see it through to the end of the revolution, we’re preparing something special. 
On second thought, special is probably only one of the words we could use to describe it. It’s also going to be:

Mind-blowing? Probably.
Bizarre? For sure.
Cosmic-horror-body-horror-terrifying? Hell yeah!
Muddy? Wait, what…

Liberté finale will see all of the characters pushed against the wall, in the most turning point since the appearance of Lady Bliss in Paris. Needless to say, you guys will have the final saying in how the story ends - and it’s going to be one tough choice to make. 

Aside from that, the translation itself is still an ongoing process – our plan is to collect requests concerning localisations and build a list of languages we should be bringing to you, step by step. Since the decision has not yet been made, you can also help move the needle: If you want to help out, Wishlist our game or join our discord. Each Wishlist includes information on the language (based on location), which adds this valuable information. Also, we will be sending out a survey soon!



Patch 0.16: Final patch before the release

Tick, tock, tick, tock… Time’s getting closer to the release!
Patch 0.16 will be the final patch before the full version arrives. It’s mainly focused on minor game improvements and bug fixes. If you have any suggestions regarding the gameplay or new features, let us know now, so we can evaluate them and prepare a task list to implement the most valid ones in this very patch.

Release Date

This is also the first time we’re talking about the release window. We’re aiming for a Q2/Q3 Full Release, but as you know – based on your feedback and our production plan, this is the perfect spot to fulfill our promises and push Liberte out from Early Access, finalizing the 1.0 version.

That doesn’t mean we’re going to stop there! We have a long list of features we’d like to implement in the game, but right now, we need to focus on delivering the above roadmap. As usual, we thank you for playing, supporting us, and providing feedback. 

We’re keen to hear from you, too - share your thoughts about the plans and tell us which update gets you hyped!

notes.title: Announcement: Focus on story & gameplay polishing in December & January
notes.content:
Bonjour Mesdames et Messieurs. We have a message for all of you who braved the streets of Paris since Liberté entered Early Access.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/7882b599b51f989bc9c7b7ed9e7fa780f3c70e34.jpg

As you know, we're very close with our community and always try to understand and meet your needs. That’s why we have decided to open the gates of Early Access and invite many of you to the community-driven development process to have a direct approach to task management in line with people's needs. 

For a team of five, meeting your expectations takes a lot of time and work. Most of our actions and improvements to the game come from your feedback, and we are glad to say that this input is much appreciated and primarily valuable.

Now, we would like to shed some light on where our focus is and what changes we are introducing.

Note: We have updated this announcement to better portray the changes we are introducing. TL:DR, our focus until the official premiere is on polishing the game and expanding the narrative. The online co-op development is put on hold until the release; we plan to focus on it after the 1.0 version. There are no changes to the local co-op. As usual, we will be working with our community to polish the game.

Focus on the story: more dynamic narrative, new dialogues, lore collectibles

One of the key areas that we plan to develop in these final moments before leaving Early Access is to expand and polish the storytelling aspect of Liberté. Our writer - Kajetan - is planning to expand all the arcs and deliver a great finale for you to experience. We are planning to release the planned roadmap in a matter of days, but here's a sneak peek:


 A more dynamic narrative. Due to some big changes in the way the narrative works, we are able to have scenes starring more characters, add more linear events, and open gates to side stories.
 Expanded lore. The next patch updates will bring a lot of new content, including lore-related collectibles.
 Hundreds of new dialogues. That's right. We are adding lots of new stuff, with the plot finally revealing the truth behind Lady Bliss and what's the endgame for the revolution.


We honestly can't wait to see it live!

Online Co-op update: further development on hold until the release of version 1.0 & available on another Steam branch 

We curiously observed different statistics on where Liberté brings the most fun. Data showed us not only your preferences gameplay-wise but also what parts of the games are most appreciated and which require some polishing (how do you like the new dodge, btw?). So, only 6% of all revolutionists tried our online co-op feature. While we appreciate the interest, we see many difficulties in providing constant support for that mode. Multiplayer bugs are twice as difficult to reproduce and way harder to fix without sacrificing our performance toward expanding Liberté's content and ensuring the road to the final release goes smoothly.

As a result, we have decided to put the development of the online co-op until the release of the 1.0 version. 

Let's make it clear that we're not abandoning this idea of online co-op. Our solution is to leave the online function in a separate build, allowing players to switch to a different branch in the Steam properties. That way, if you want, you can still have fun with online co-op. This change will go live the day we ship the patch planned for January. We wanted to give you a heads-up so that the change won't happen overnight.

We want to put our efforts into something significantly more important, which will impact the game's final state. Our dream is to make Liberté one of the best roguelite games, and we believe it will happen with your support.

Our early plans for getting back to this idea are somewhere between Patch 1.1 and 1.2 after the final release. Leaving Early Access is on the horizon, and depending on how the launch goes and how many people will ask for this particular mode, we plan to revisit the idea of developing the online co-op further.

As always, you're the fire to our revolution

On a final note, we are humbled and overwhelmed by your positive vibes, whether on the Discord channel, Steam Review, and Community Center or offline events like Gamescom or PAX West. No sugar coating here - your support fuels the creation of every line of code, dialogue, and asset. We want to thank you for your continuous support and for helping us make Liberté a cool game!

Talk to you soon!
SuperStatic Studio

notes.title: Dev Diary - learn the story behind SuperStatic Studio!
notes.content:
Revolutionists!

It's time we revealed at least a part of the mystery - who we are, why we created Liberté, and what inspired us. So, before we got to this point below…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/161989202487b7e5712ec2c1e13788e69eb4ac8d.jpg

Way before SuperStatic Studio got its name; two friends worked together in a start-up - UX Designer Daniel and Marketing Specialist Kajetan. When the pandemic hit - yes, it's one of these Covid-19 stories - we got together and started discussing creating a game. The only thing we knew was the genre.

After a few rum-filled glasses (one of our favorite drinks), we started workshopping, going over ideas on the most remarkable story we could come up with. We both thought there was something very appealing in making a game set in a historical setting, but with our imaginary twist.

One of the early drafts of the story included an aquatic world that's supposedly at war with an on-the-surface civilization (that might have been the direct influence of watching Aquaman). Still, after heated debates, the concept was discarded.

The concept of a political hotpot was nonetheless what eventually stuck for the longest, and we explored this further. One angle we started exploring was the significant events in history when several groups clashed, and nothing could beat the French Revolution. As we educated ourselves on the proceedings, the idea of bringing voodoo to the mix was born. This was, in fact, the effect of our extensive research - the Haiti Revolution in particular. That's how we arrived at creating The Congregation and The Tribe.

From that point, we brainstormed on the main threat looming on the horizon - the arch-nemesis of all the groups involved in the conflict. Eventually, we got in the vibe of cosmic horror, influenced by movies such as Annihiliation (2018) or The Fly (1986) or even more obscure ones like Matango (1963). One breadcrumb led to another, and we ended up with the prototypes of the Bliss - strange cosmic gardens where you'd play against zombies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4e44ce6af8981ad9886919668e15fa73a2243b5d.jpg

After giving it a play, we lacked a powerful embodiment of this other horror dimension. We bounced ideas - a dragon, an alien invasion - and hence Lady Bliss was born. The goal was to make Liberté's horrors a "horrid beauty."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/e43e3451df3e8d229481049d1c901cf8bfd57497.png

Each faction was described along with the symbols and artifacts, such as the masks of the Tribesmen. Here's an excerpt about their meaning from the notes about the Tribe's religion:

"A reference to Guardian Ori from Yoruba beliefs, as well as Torado in the religion of the Wilderpeople. The Wilderpeople used to carry painted skulls of their ancestors as their protectors. Since the practice was widely criticized in the modern world, the custom changed to wearing colorful masks on their faces or attached to their belts or other parts of the garment. These bones and skulls represent the connection to the souls which have been cleansed and sent back to Earth by Torado."

Rumors say there's enough lore made for Liberté that we could quickly write a book on that!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/4d44f59dad6a6f04f54582041d57263bb8956875.jpg

Once the concept was more or less finalized, Daniel started the development, while Kajetan got into the writing vibe. We collaborated closely on each new part of the Liberté world. Here's one of the first views of a street where we tested the AI of our enemies and the crowd that populated Paris.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/cc8cca465db85ce465c2ccd1d1cbdda830105120.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/2c1ed7d971103786738d3090fe38dd6724052f83.jpg

SuperStatic Studio has worked with highly talented people since Liberté started to gain some shape.

Ania, our leading artist, worked with us on bringing all the characters to life.

From briefs to inspiration boards and early sketches, Ania has turned our ideas into beautiful art we see today in the game.

Like it happened with Archbishop de Maury, the mysterious spiritual leader of the Congregation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/bac9f77933efb7ca88b9d4ff0f40eade557aafa8.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/c4363e1f2af515dd5eb98db9696b638564b85046.jpg

Luca and Wojtek designed the streets and locations you see today in the game. Their work was based on accurate maps and research on the look of 18th-century Paris.

Here's a bird's eye view of one of the maps in the game's early development.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/08c02695ed9e07731c97257f0e01105c22bc59f7.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/bddd11f1d46ae2cf3e8eab3524b21da053223234.jpg

We're fortunate to have worked with such a wildly talented bunch, and they're part of our family.

Thanks to this collaborative work, we've managed to go from this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/46dae4317cbf4792b2830ea920e46199c164fbd9.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a7b622fbe192b376728708b6c5399ac6c00d44d8.jpg

To this:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/ec6201109f74c765a6eaea8914ec98400ba2f64d.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/9e670c913eeef7ec38be07dec5ab2fb6aa96784e.jpg

Over the last two years, Liberté grew into a publisher-backed game that blends roguelite and roguelike mechanisms in a unique setting.

On a personal note from the devs - it's genuinely our dream coming true - getting a chance to create something that a growing community will enjoy diving into. While we tirelessly work on developing and polishing Liberté, we're always thankful for your continuous support.

That's our brief story. Let us know in the comments if there's anything else you'd like to read about.

notes.title: Superstatic X Anshar Publishing

notes.title: Dev update #3 - Meet Lady Bliss
notes.content:
Hi!

With September arriving, we're ready to show you - and cast more light too - on our main antagonist of Liberte, Lady Bliss.

This character was firstly designed as "a colossal monster, covered in mushrooms and plants, bearing some resemblance to a human being". From that point onwards, we've been iterating the idea, working on e enhancements and building a key character of the narrative.

Lady Bliss is an extremely intelligent being that arrives at Paris (seemingly) out of nowhere. In the beginning, we won't reveal her origins, and her entire backstory is only known after you've discovered the narrative of all factions - then, the pieces of the puzzle finally align. Lady Bliss can communicate with selected people through telekinesis, and she's responsible for the Bliss that spreads in Paris - the intricate maze of strange, mystic gardens that pop up in the city. 

People, who enter the Bliss become infected, and achieve a horrifying version of nirvana. What they begin to experience is pure joy, but that's Lady Bliss sedating them, only to turn them into part of this massive biomass she uses to grow.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/065acd8221952bd4a539b53d9266636b326511f9.png

Given our inspirations rooted in the works of H.P. Lovecraft, Lady Bliss represents some of the features commonly known in cosmic horrors in terms of her appearance too. Notice her tentacles, and how she uses her victims to literally construct her own body. At the same time, she's one with nature, therefore the unique combination of human flesh, plants, and fungus tissue in her design.

Some say that the monster come from the hell below, while others believe it's a God that came to Paris to wash away the sins of the royalty.

As found in the notes of one of the Parisians who witnessed Lady Bliss' arrival:

"Nothing scared me more than this walking wrath. It's been sent by the Gods, or might even be one. People were like toys for it, as it walked among the houses and churches, turning everything green, lush, leaving a scent of flowers and joy. But I've seen what it did to people - they lost their minds, took their clothes off, and started dancing around the wicked trees, made of plants and humans. Trembling and terrified, I hid, there's chaos in the city now. 

I know that.

We are lost."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/a653e2a1544f7d765f534b36d5e25a7b66903ad2.gif

notes.title: Dev Update #2 - Rebels HQ is ready!
notes.content:
Hey there Revolutionists!

Summer's been busy, so here's a sneak peek into one of the things we've been working on. Our first player's HQ, the Theatre that was taken over by the Rebels shortly after the revolution started in Paris, was recently designed and polished.

From the start, we've been aiming for a burlesque look, inspired by the interior design of the 19th century France, as well as the over-the-top look of the 1950s and the bizarre burlesque-inspired shows. We wanted this place to capture Ana Tallien's zaniness, but also provide a climatic setting for the players who choose to support Rebels.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/5efb43a1a1aebc4ce654b2c930358fc4c9cc426a.gif

Since Liberte is a roguelike, this is the spot where your character will respawn after the run ends. In the Early Access version, we're planning to keep the Theatre as the main HQ for all runs, however, as the game will expand, we plan to build one such HQ for each of the factions.

In this newly designed HQ, we wanted the foyer to be in ruins, barricaded and guarded by the Rebels. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/b01aef063a5f73c97f300d6cf5d91aee8f2f7b97.png

The interior part, the main hall, is where the Rebels Leader Ana Tallien hides, along with her brain of the operations, Max The Professor. The lighting focuses on Max's plans, and this place will be busy with their henchmen preparing booby traps and weapons to fuel the rebellion. Take a look at Ana preaching the rebellion's virtues below.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40312711/7bf91771e08962651a435bb3fd5e958837e82f75.png

Much of the work revolved around volumetric lights, creating the effect of dim, steamy interiors. From the game design perspective, the Theatre's located in the city centre, and will be transformed as you guys progress with the story.

More updates coming soon!

Let's keep in touch via our Discord.
